brief: Trade was choppy overnight. The yen strengthened on more hawkish BOJ repricing and intervention speculation, pressuring exporters, with a modest bid elsewhere after energy and rates eased. ADP printed +38k versus +47k expected, reinforcing the cooler labor tone from JOLTS, and NFP Friday is the main event. Williams pushed back on a September hike, helping rates and gold. Waller speaks today, and softer labor data gives him room to lean dovish. Privorotsky reads the recent hawkish tone as Warsh retaining credibility rather than a committee shift. On AI he argues frontier competition, Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 and speculation on Astra, is compressing cost per token, with the Silicon Data token index down 29% in August. Consumption must then grow faster than prices fall, so absent radical capability jumps compute oversupply becomes plausible, which alongside credit repricing explains the sector de-rating. Broadcom beat in Q3, guided roughly $115bn FY27 and $230bn FY28 AI revenue, but Q4 revenue came slightly below the Street. Snowflake was cleaner. He expects escalate to de-escalate on Iran, places energy nearer the high end of its near-term range with oil above $90, and holds that markets are stable or higher as long as energy does not rise.
